_note: Policy claims copied from each person's own Meta ads (public Ad Library, read 2026-10-13). One claim = one position a voter could use.

people.name: Isak Asare
claims: C1: focus on more affordable and attainable housing
C2: increased economic opportunities
C3: immediate climate action

people.name: Taylor Wishau
people.seat: Racine County WI Board Supervisor District 21 (Burlington area; 2022 race)
claims: C1: increase funding and support for law enforcement; do not micromanage the police budget
C2: increase public access to county Health and Human Services (Burlington office)
C3: business partnerships to attract jobs to Burlington / western Racine County; control property taxes
C4: expand programs and services for veterans

people.name: Jacob Wood
claims: C1: end predatory towing / fix the parking crisis
C2: take on over-occupancy of housing
C3: lower property taxes / stop tax increases
C4: restore transparency in city government
C5: protect the lake (Utah Lake)
C6: push for discussions on a UVU football stadium in Vineyard

people.name: Emily Lockhart
people.seat: Lehi UT city council (2025 race; also ran Utah Senate 22 in 2024)
claims: C1: transportation plan - more east-west connections, including connecting Pony Express Parkway to the Vineyard connector
C2: strengthen public safety (endorsed by firefighters and FOP)
C3: guide strategic growth
C4: limited government, fiscal responsibility, individual liberty

people.name: Marsha Judkins
people.seat: Provo UT mayor (2025 race; former state House District 61)
claims: C1: fix outdated permitting and licensing systems
C2: update Provo's Master Plan; reverse declining sales tax revenue with neighborhood-focused growth
C3: support and revitalize downtown
C4: (as legislator) voted against SB 2001, which would have raised taxes on gas and groceries
C5: advocate for local control, limited government, less regulation

people.name: Katrice MacKay
claims: C1: zoning should reflect each neighborhood's own concerns; pledge to listen to every neighborhood on projects
C2: keep parks beautiful and well maintained
C3: a smartphone app to communicate with the city / 311
C4: a stated position on the future of Slate Canyon (in a video; text says only 'where I stand')

people.name: David Spencer
people.seat: Utah County UT Commissioner (former Orem city council)
claims: C1: no tax increases; county should live within its means
C2: no commissioner pay raises
C3: oppose bigger county budgets and higher fees

people.name: Nithya Raman
people.seat: Los Angeles city council D4; candidate for LA mayor 2026
claims: C1: capped rent increases for over a million Angelenos (claims credit for a rent-cap action)
C2: plan to lower the cost of housing
C3: City Hall insiders, the landlord lobby and the LAPD have run city politics (critique of LAPD influence)

people.name: Karen Bass
claims: C1: opposes ICE / federal immigration raids in LA
C2: encampments cleared, thousands housed (Inside Safe)
C3: signed Executive Directive 1 (ED1) to speed up affordable housing
C4: fighting red tape and insurers (wildfire recovery)

people.name: Lana Negrete
people.seat: Santa Monica CA city council (2026 re-election)
claims: C1: public safety, including safety on public transit
C2: homelessness, mental health and drug addiction services
C3: housing affordability ('who is housing actually affordable for?')
C4: economic recovery / support small business
